instances.claim: This tells me that there is a bounded, already-introduced collection of individual works called Cents, whose membership is fixed, so that a claim can be made about every member of it.
instances.why: "Every Cent" quantifies over a population the draft has never established: lines 1–10 introduce only the currency ("one cent", "Lincoln cents", "a cent") and a single readymade, never a set of titled works, and the only bounding figure — "ten thousand inscriptions, and never any more" — arrives six lines later at 17, with the title CENTS itself appearing for the first time at 20. The universal claim is therefore being made about a set the audience has not yet been given, and it reads as settled because "every" always does.
